submitted.rationale: Index 13 (Bi0.75Sb0.25, the Bi3SbO7 composition) gave the highest measured EQE, 2.46e-4 %. MACE puts Bi3SbO7 on the hull, and MEGNet predicts an HSE gap of 2.27 eV, below the 2.4 eV photon energy, so it can absorb this light. The neighbouring compositions on both sides measured lower.

rejected.reason: Sillenite Bi12SbO20 region; measured EQE 1.40e-4 %, lower than index 13
Bi3SbO7 + BiSbO4 mixture; measured EQE 1.44e-4 %, lower than index 13
Predicted gap is 3.06 eV, above the 2.4 eV photon energy, so it should barely absorb

consultations.verdict: Support: Bi3SbO7 (Sb 0.25) is on the MACE hull and MEGNet HSE gap 2.27 eV < 2.4 eV photon energy, so it absorbs; BiSbO4 (3.06 eV) would not absorb. Index 13 (Sb 0.249) sits on the Bi3SbO7 stoichiometry.

Support: sillenite Bi12SbO20 (Sb 0.077) is near-hull (0.019 eV/atom) with a predicted gap (1.68 eV HSE) well below 2.4 eV, so it absorbs strongly. Index 5 (Sb 0.080) matches this composition. Bi3SbO7 at index 13 gave a very low EQE.

Mixed. BiSbO4 is on the hull but has a wide gap (3.06 eV), so it won't absorb at 2.4 eV. Index 16 (Sb 0.35) should be a Bi3SbO7 + BiSbO4 mixture, which could form a heterojunction that improves charge separation beyond Bi3SbO7 alone. EQE was higher at Sb 0.25 than at 0.08, which points toward the Sb-rich side. The GP-UCB also picks index 16.
